qt: to the Commission Anthony Smith (The Left) Subject:

In 2025, 24.2 % of people in the EU aged 15 to 29 were at risk of poverty or social exclusion. The reinforced Youth Guarantee, which focuses on getting young people into work, does not actually guarantee any income. Its implementation has also been uneven, as Parliament highlighted in its resolution of 15 September 2026. In France, both the National Union of Students of France and the Student Union have called for a youth autonomy allowance that would be at least equal to the poverty threshold. They have also demanded that student grants be indexed to inflation and calculated according to students’ own financial means, rather than their parents’. These demands suggest there could be scope for introducing a European social pillar that would include all young people – students, trainees, apprentices and young jobseekers – without requiring them to find employment first or be financially dependent on their families. 1.

Is the Commission considering an initiative to harmonise upwards the Member States’ income support schemes for young adults, including students, centred around a youth autonomy allowance set above the poverty threshold in each Member State, which would be automatically indexed to inflation and adjusted for the cost of living?
What European instruments and funding will it put in place to ensure this pillar can work effectively all year round, maintain personalised support and reduce inequalities between the Member States?
